content.text: The key thing is "at specified path" which means it's a system-scoped dependency. Let me check oss-parent-7 more carefully:

content.content:
<url>https://oss.sonatype.org/service/local/staging/deploy/maven2/</url>
		</repository>
	</distributionManagement>

	<build>
		<plugins>
			<plugin>
				<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
				<artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
				<version>1.0</version>
				<executions>
					<execution>
						<id>enforce-maven</id>
						<goals>
							<goal>enforce</goal>
						</goals>
						<configuration>
							<rules>
								<requireMavenVersion>
									<version>(,2.1.0),(2.1.0,2.2.0),(2.2.0,)</version>
									<message>Maven 2.1.0 and 2.2.0 produce incorrect GPG signatures and checksums respectively.</message>
								</requireMavenVersion>
							</rules>
						</configuration>
					</execution>
				</executions>
			</plugin>
		</plugins>
		<pluginManagement>
			<plugins>
				<plugin>
					<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
					<artifactId>maven-release-plugin</artifactId>
					<version>2.1</version>
					<configuration>
						<mavenExecutorId>forked-path</mavenExecutorId>
						<useReleaseProfile>false</useReleaseProfile>
						<arguments>-Psonatype-oss-release</arguments>
					</configuration>
				</plugin>
			</plugins>
		</pluginManagement>
	</build>

	<properties>
		<project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
		<sonatypeOssDistMgmtSnapshotsUrl>https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots/</sonatypeOssDistMgmtSnapshotsUrl>
	</properties>

	<profiles>
		<profile>
			<id>sonatype-oss-release</id>
			<build>
				<plugins>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>2.1.2</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>attach-sources</id>
								<goals>
									<goal>jar-no-fork</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>2.7</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>attach-javadocs</id>
								<goals>
									<goal>jar</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>1.1</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>sign-artifacts</id>
								<phase>verify</phase>
								<goals>
									<goal>sign</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
				</plugins>
			</build>
		</profile>

Modify the parent POM (pom.xml) to add a profile for Java 9+ that properly
handles the absence of tools.jar. Since Java 9+, the tools are built-in to the

After fixing the tools.jar issue, the factory module fails with:
"cannot find symbol: class Generated in package javax.annotation"

This occurs because in Java 9+, javax.annotation.Generated was removed from the JDK
and must be provided as an external dependency (javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api).

The factory module imports javax.annotation.Generated but doesn't declare

There are two problems to fix:

   Add exclusions to eliminate the com.sun:tools dependency that compile-testing

   - compile-testing:0.6/0.8 declares com.sun:tools with system scope
   - compile-testing tries to find it at ${toolsjar}
   - But on Java 11, tools.jar doesn't exist

   - service/pom.xml
   - factory/pom.xml
   - value/pom.xml

2. JAVAX.ANNOTATION.GENERATED MISSING (Secondary):
   The factory module needs javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api as a dependency.

   SOLUTION: Add javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api dependency to factory/pom.xml

Both are BUILD CONFIGURATION ISSUES, not source code issues.

BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS - Google Auto Repository
==============================================

FAILED BUILD MODULES:
- service (auto-service)
- factory (auto-factory)
- value (auto-value)
- common (auto-common) - potentially also affected

ROOT CAUSE:
-----------
The build fails with the following error when trying to compile Java modules:

"Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

This is a DEPENDENCY RESOLUTION ERROR, not a code error.

ANALYSIS:
---------
The parent POM (pom.xml) defines profiles that attempt to locate tools.jar:

1. default-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (typical Linux/Windows)
2. mac-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (macOS)

These profiles define a property <toolsjar> that points to the location of tools.jar.

PROBLEM:
The child modules (service, factory, value) do NOT have explicit dependency declarations
for com.sun:tools in their POM files. However, somewhere in the dependency chain
(likely inherited through compile-testing or another transitive dependency), a
dependency on com.sun:tools is being pulled in with a path-based system scope.

In Java 9+, tools.jar was removed and its contents merged into the main JDK. The
path ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar does NOT exist in Java 11, causing Maven to fail
when it tries to resolve this system-scoped dependency.

MODULES AFFECTED:
1. auto-service/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.6 (test dependency)
2. auto-factory/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.8 (test dependency)
3. auto-value/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.6 (test dependency)

we need to prevent Maven from trying to resolve the non-existent com.sun:tools
dependency.

A) Add explicit exclusions in the modules that depend on compile-testing
B) Configure the parent POM to properly handle Java 9+ where tools.jar doesn't exist

Modify the parent POM (pom.xml) to add a profile for Java 9+ that properly
handles the absence of tools.jar. Since Java 9+, the tools are built-in to the
JDK, so we should NOT activate the profile that tries to add tools.jar as a
dependency on Java 9+.

The fix involves:
1. Updating the default-profile activation condition to exclude Java 9+
2. Potentially adding profile exclusion for when tools.jar path does not exist

    22→
    23→1. default-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (typical Linux/Windows)
    24→2. mac-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (macOS)

    31→(likely inherited through compile-testing or another transitive dependency), a
    32→dependency on com.sun:tools is being pulled in with a path-based system scope.
    33→
    34→In Java 9+, tools.jar was removed and its contents merged into the main JDK. The
    35→path ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar does NOT exist in Java 11, causing Maven to fail
    36→when it tries to resolve this system-scoped dependency.

    40→2. auto-factory/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.8 (test dependency)

    47→Since Java 9+/11 no longer has/needs tools.jar (its classes are in the base JVM),
    48→we need to prevent Maven from trying to resolve the non-existent com.sun:tools
    49→dependency.

    62→The factory module imports javax.annotation.Generated but doesn't declare

BUILD ERROR ANALYSIS - Google Auto Repository
==============================================

FAILED BUILD MODULES:
- service (auto-service)
- factory (auto-factory)
- value (auto-value)
- common (auto-common) - potentially also affected

ROOT CAUSE:
-----------
The build fails with the following error when trying to compile Java modules:

"Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

This is a DEPENDENCY RESOLUTION ERROR, not a code error.

ANALYSIS:
---------
The parent POM (pom.xml) defines profiles that attempt to locate tools.jar:

1. default-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (typical Linux/Windows)
2. mac-profile: Looks for ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (macOS)

These profiles define a property <toolsjar> that points to the location of tools.jar.

PROBLEM:
The child modules (service, factory, value) do NOT have explicit dependency declarations
for com.sun:tools in their POM files. However, somewhere in the dependency chain
(likely inherited through compile-testing or another transitive dependency), a
dependency on com.sun:tools is being pulled in with a path-based system scope.

In Java 9+, tools.jar was removed and its contents merged into the main JDK. The
path ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar does NOT exist in Java 11, causing Maven to fail
when it tries to resolve this system-scoped dependency.

MODULES AFFECTED:
1. auto-service/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.6 (test dependency)
2. auto-factory/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.8 (test dependency)
3. auto-value/pom.xml - Uses compile-testing:0.6 (test dependency)

These compile-testing dependencies likely transitively depend on tools.jar being available.

FIX STRATEGY:
-------------
Since Java 9+/11 no longer has/needs tools.jar (its classes are in the base JVM),
we need to prevent Maven from trying to resolve the non-existent com.sun:tools
dependency.

There are two approaches:
A) Add explicit exclusions in the modules that depend on compile-testing
B) Configure the parent POM to properly handle Java 9+ where tools.jar doesn't exist

SECONDARY ERROR - javax.annotation.Generated Missing:
After fixing the tools.jar issue, the factory module fails with:
"cannot find symbol: class Generated in package javax.annotation"

This occurs because in Java 9+, javax.annotation.Generated was removed from the JDK
and must be provided as an external dependency (javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api).

The factory module imports javax.annotation.Generated but doesn't declare
this dependency.

RECOMMENDED FIX:
There are two problems to fix:

1. TOOLS.JAR ISSUE (Primary):
   Add exclusions to eliminate the com.sun:tools dependency that compile-testing
   transitively requires. This dependency path was:
   - compile-testing:0.6/0.8 declares com.sun:tools with system scope
   - compile-testing tries to find it at ${toolsjar}
   - But on Java 11, tools.jar doesn't exist

   SOLUTION: Add <exclusions> to compile-testing dependencies in:
   - service/pom.xml
   - factory/pom.xml
   - value/pom.xml

2. JAVAX.ANNOTATION.GENERATED MISSING (Secondary):
   The factory module needs javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api as a dependency.

   SOLUTION: Add javax.annotation:javax.annotation-api dependency to factory/pom.xml

Both are BUILD CONFIGURATION ISSUES, not source code issues.
